/SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Issued at 250 AM EDT Fri Jul 24 2026

This Weekend...

Upper ridging from the western CONUS starts to build more into the 
central CONUS this weekend with general troughing from the eastern 
Great Lakes into New England. We'll be situated between these two 
features with our upper flow orienting to a more NW flow aloft type 
of setup. At the surface, high pressure will start to lose influence 
over our area, and a frontal boundary will lift northward toward the 
TN Valley as a weak warm front. PWAT values will surge up around 2" 
through the column as we get into Saturday, and again on Sunday. In 
addition, instability will build into our area the second half of 
the weekend as the eastern periphery of the upper ridge gets more 
established across the central CONUS into the mid Mississippi River 
Valley. Overall, deep layer shear on Saturday isn't overly 
impressive, at least in the lower levels. Above 500 mb, we will have 
the exit region of a notable mid to upper level impulse, however H85 
winds are more likely to be 10 knots or less. Regardless of the 
shear profile, the environment looks mostly capped, so only expect 
some isolated to widely scattered shower chances below the inversion 
for Friday night into Saturday mainly across southern and western KY.

By Sunday, overall, deep layer shear profiles should improve some, 
but will still be fairly weak below 500 mb. Forecast soundings look 
less capped by this time, and suggest that some strong instability 
on the order of 3000-4000 J/KG of CAPE could develop. It is possible 
some strong to severe storms could develop on this day, however most 
of the deterministic data doesn't have much of a trigger to key in 
on. Will keep an optimistic forecast going for now given that lack 
of a confident trigger, and focus more on the building heat and 
humidity for this time. Forecast highs are expected to surge back 
into the upper 80s and around 90 assuming we stay mostly dry. In 
addition, dew points are expected to recover to the low and mid 70s 
for most of the CWA (minus the Bluegrass counties). This could put 
max afternoon heat indices back in the 95 to 100 degree range along 
and west of I-65.

Early Monday - Late Tuesday...

Our NW flow aloft pattern will hold over the area through at least 
the middle of next week with strong upper ridging dominating the 
western and central CONUS, and troughing over the eastern Great 
Lakes and New England. We'll likely keep plenty of instability 
across our area thanks to the eastern periphery of the upper ridge. 
In addition, deep layer shear will be somewhat enhanced by the mid 
to upper level jet structure nosing SE into our region. Models 
continue to hint at a shortwave or two embedded in the NW flow aloft 
upstream of us in the early Monday through late Tuesday time frame, 
and these could be a trigger for some MCS activity upstream of us 
that could potentially forward propagate into our area. The overall 
pattern does have that look, but overall the run to run data has 
been consistently inconsistent with any key features. We'll have to 
keep an eye on the Monday/Tuesday time frame for potential MCS 
activity riding into our area between the mean 700-300 mb flow and 
NNW to SSE oriented instability gradients. It is possible the bulk 
of any MCS activity stays to our north and east, but it is also 
plausible to get a forward propagating/cold pool enhanced complex to 
work into our area from the north. We'll keep monitoring, especially 
across our NE CWA where most of the activity should track if it 
occurs. Wouldn't be surprised to see an eventual outlook over our 
area, particularly for the Monday time frame.

For now, the bigger story will be the heat and humidity with Mon/Tue 
high temperatures expected to reach the lower 90s combined with low 
and mid 70s dew points across much of the area. Along and west of I-
65 our max HI values could reach the 105+ range, and some Heat 
Advisory headlines appear possible for these two days. One caveat 
would be if we do get MCS activity to wreck the temp forecast either 
of these days.

Wednesday - Thursday...

Actually have higher confidence in the mid week outlook as the upper 
pattern should remain the same. However, data agrees that the NW 
flow aloft will be more void of any notable triggers, and surface 
high pressure builds back into the area behind a passing cool front 
or convectively reinforced cold pool from the early week concerns. 
Looking for a drier and slightly cooler forecast as highs return 
back to the upper 80s to near 90.
